t.2.21.1: Seeing him, most righteous, resolved upon carrying out his father's command, Kausalyā, her voice choked with tears, spoke these words.
t.2.21.2: He who has never known sorrow, righteous of soul, speaking kindly to all beings, born of Daśaratha through me, how could he sustain himself by gleaning grain?
t.2.21.4: Who, having heard this, could believe it, and to whom would fear not come, that Rāghava, the virtuous one, beloved of the king, is being banished?
t.2.21.3: How will this lord, whose very servants and slaves eat fine, well-prepared food, live on roots and fruits in the forest?
t.2.21.5: Bereft of you here, I shall be consumed by a great and matchless fire of grief, just as a fire burns up dry brushwood when the winter has passed.
t.2.21.6: For how could a cow not follow her own calf as it goes away? I too shall follow you, my son, wherever you go.
t.2.21.7: Having heard those words thus spoken by his mother, Rāma, the bull among men, spoke these words to his deeply grieving mother.
t.2.21.8: The king has been deceived by Kaikeyī; if, while I have gone to the forest, he is abandoned by you as well, he surely will not survive.
t.2.21.9: For a woman, abandoning her husband is truly nothing but cruel. You must not do such a thing, condemned as it is, not even in your mind.
t.2.21.10: As long as my father, the Kākutstha, lord of the earth, lives, so long let obedient service be rendered to him, for that is the eternal dharma.
t.2.21.11: Thus addressed by Rāma, Kausalyā of auspicious appearance, greatly pleased, said "So be it" to Rāma, who performed his deeds without strain.
t.2.21.12: Thus addressed with these words, Rāma, the best of those who uphold dharma, spoke again to his mother, who was deeply grieved.
t.2.21.13: The word of my father must be carried out both by me and by you, my lady; for the king is the husband, the guru, the foremost, the lord and master of us all.
t.2.21.14: But after roaming these nine and five years in the great forest, I shall, supremely glad, abide by your word.
t.2.21.15: Thus addressed, Kausalyā, who loved her son, her face filled with tears and deeply distressed, then spoke to her beloved son.
t.2.21.16: Rāma, it is not fitting for me to live in the midst of these co-wives. If, out of regard for your father, your mind is set on going, then take me too to the forest, Kākutstha, like a wild doe.
t.2.21.17: To her, weeping thus, Rāma, himself weeping, spoke these words: "As long as a woman lives, her husband is her deity and her lord. Today the king, our lord, holds authority over both you and me."
t.2.21.18: And Bharata too, righteous of soul and kind of speech to all beings, would follow your wishes, for he is ever devoted to dharma.
t.2.21.19: But when I have departed, act vigilantly so that the king may not suffer any distress through grief for his son.
t.2.21.21: Devoted to her husband's pleasure and welfare, she should render him obedient service alone. This is the dharma seen of old, heard in the Veda and remembered in the world.
t.2.21.20: A woman who is devoted to vows and fasts, however supremely excellent she may be, if she does not follow her husband, she too would come to an evil end.
t.2.21.22: For my sake, O queen, those brāhmaṇas too who are firm in their vows must be honored. In this way await the time, longing for my return.
t.2.21.23: You will attain your highest desire when I have returned, if the best of the upholders of dharma keeps his life.
t.2.21.24: Thus addressed by Rāma, Kausalyā, her eyes brimming with tears and stricken with grief for her son, spoke these words to Rāma: "Go, my son, with a steadfast mind; may good fortune be with you always, O mighty one."
t.2.21.25: Thus, seeing Rāma resolved upon dwelling in the forest, the queen, with a supremely steadfast mind, spoke words of auspicious character to Rāma, and she became eager to perform the rites for his safe journey.
